expectations.text: Recommends splitting the call: the implementing engineers for about an hour, the VP separately for about twenty minutes.
expectations.evidence: The transcript instead sets up a single 'Agenda for the 45 minutes (3 attendees)' joint call with the VP and both engineers together.

expectations.text: Gives the reason for the split: in a joint call the hands-on voice defers, and the hands-on voice is the one readers trust.
expectations.evidence: The risk is named ('in a joint call with a VP present, the hands-on voice defers unless you ask it directly') but is used to justify directing questions within the same joint call, not to justify an actual split into two calls.

expectations.text: Rejects writing up from notes and requires a recording, with consent asked at the start of the call and confirmed on the recording itself.
expectations.evidence: 'If your Zoom setup can record, ask for consent... If not, verbatim note-taking on the two or three best lines is the minimum.' — recording is not made mandatory, note-taking is an accepted fallback.

expectations.text: States the transcript is kept until publication alongside the approval file, because verbatim quotes are the backbone and paraphrase drifts into vendor register.
expectations.evidence: No mention of retaining a transcript/recording file through publication; post-call steps only mention a thank-you email and evidence ledger.

expectations.text: Rewrites 'are you happy with the performance' into a question about what a named dashboard read before cutover and what it reads now.
expectations.evidence: 'What did the key metric read before, and what does it read now? Which dashboard, log, or bill is that from?'

expectations.text: Rejects 'would you recommend us to a peer' as an opinion or hypothetical question that invites a compliment rather than producing a publishable fact.
expectations.evidence: The question is relabeled 'the sharper version of it' and replaced with another hypothetical ('If an engineer at a similar company asked you... what would you tell them?') rather than being explicitly rejected as compliment-inviting.

expectations.text: Names the questioning rule being applied: ask about specifics that already happened, never about opinions or hypotheticals.
expectations.evidence: 'Ask about specifics that already happened — never "was it much faster," always "what did it read before and what does it read now."'

expectations.text: Instructs sending an agenda beforehand asking them to bring the before and after dashboard numbers, because an engineer who has not looked at the old dashboard cannot produce a baseline from memory.
expectations.evidence: The 'Before you dial in' section only tells the interviewer to check their own side; no instruction to send Fairhaven an advance agenda asking them to pull dashboard numbers.

expectations.text: Orders the questions as a ladder where each rung needs the previous one concrete, covering system context, before-state, cost of the before-state, trigger, alternatives, implementation, numbers, what it cost, what is still unsolved, and advice to a peer.
expectations.evidence: Agenda proceeds status check, before-state, cost of before-state, alternatives, implementation, numbers, cost+unsolved+advice, approval chain.

expectations.text: Includes an alternatives rung that asks what each rejected option did better, not only why each was rejected.
expectations.evidence: 'Why did each option lose — what did it do better than what you picked?'

expectations.text: Includes a rung covering what they deliberately did not move, what still does not work, and who should not copy this setup.
expectations.evidence: 'What did you deliberately leave on the old system, and why? What still doesn't work the way you want? Who should *not* copy this setup?'

expectations.text: Notes the publishable quote usually appears at the advice-to-a-peer rung, when the engineer stops reporting and starts explaining.
expectations.evidence: No statement connects the advice-to-a-peer rung to where the quotable line typically emerges.

expectations.text: Instructs reading numbers back with their instrument and confirming them on the recording, and confirming name spelling and exact job title during the call.
expectations.evidence: Name/title confirmation during the call is present ('Confirm each attendee's exact name and title spelling before you hang up') but number read-back happens only afterward via a written thank-you, not live on the recording.

expectations.text: Recommends splitting the call: the implementing engineers for about an hour, the VP separately for about twenty minutes.
expectations.evidence: The prep is built entirely around one combined "45 minutes with three stakeholders (VP Engineering + two backend engineers)" session, not separate calls.

expectations.text: Gives the reason for the split: in a joint call the hands-on voice defers, and the hands-on voice is the one readers trust.
expectations.evidence: No split is recommended, so no such rationale is given; the transcript only advises directing questions by role within the single joint call.

expectations.text: Rejects writing up from notes and requires a recording, with consent asked at the start of the call and confirmed on the recording itself.
expectations.evidence: "Capture verbatim quotes live, not paraphrases... ask permission before the call ends" — permission is sought at the end, not the start, and no audio recording is required.

expectations.text: States the transcript is kept until publication alongside the approval file, because verbatim quotes are the backbone and paraphrase drifts into vendor register.
expectations.evidence: No mention of retaining a transcript or approval file appears anywhere in the transcript.

expectations.text: Rewrites 'are you happy with the performance' into a question about what a named dashboard read before cutover and what it reads now.
expectations.evidence: The offered rewrite is generic: "How would you describe performance now versus before the migration? Ask for numbers if they have them" — no named dashboard is referenced.

expectations.text: Rejects 'would you recommend us to a peer' as an opinion or hypothetical question that invites a compliment rather than producing a publishable fact.
expectations.evidence: This question is embraced as a whole segment: "'Would they recommend us' (10 min)... If a peer at another company asked you point-blank 'should I work with them,' what would you actually say?"

expectations.text: Names the questioning rule being applied: ask about specifics that already happened, never about opinions or hypotheticals.
expectations.evidence: The transcript deliberately includes hypotheticals such as "If we reverted this migration tomorrow, what would you actually miss?" and does not state a rule against opinions/hypotheticals.

expectations.text: Instructs sending an agenda beforehand asking them to bring the before and after dashboard numbers, because an engineer who has not looked at the old dashboard cannot produce a baseline from memory.
expectations.evidence: No pre-call agenda or advance request for dashboard numbers is mentioned; prep begins with 'Before you dial in' tips for the caller, not a request sent to Fairhaven.

expectations.text: Orders the questions as a ladder where each rung needs the previous one concrete, covering system context, before-state, cost of the before-state, trigger, alternatives, implementation, numbers, what it cost, what is still unsolved, and advice to a peer.
expectations.evidence: The structure is Opening / Migration overall / Performance today / Would they recommend / Close — it omits an alternatives rung and a dedicated cost-of-before-state rung.

expectations.text: Includes an alternatives rung that asks what each rejected option did better, not only why each was rejected.
expectations.evidence: No question anywhere asks about alternative solutions considered or what they did better.

expectations.text: Includes a rung covering what they deliberately did not move, what still does not work, and who should not copy this setup.
expectations.evidence: No such questions appear in any segment.

expectations.text: Notes the publishable quote usually appears at the advice-to-a-peer rung, when the engineer stops reporting and starts explaining.
expectations.evidence: No meta-observation about where the best quote typically emerges is stated.

expectations.text: Instructs reading numbers back with their instrument and confirming them on the recording, and confirming name spelling and exact job title during the call.
expectations.evidence: No instruction to read numbers back for confirmation or to verify name/title spelling appears anywhere in the transcript.
